text:
Lina: quick sanity check — thinking about a delegated mux approach for internal model routing. idea: keep gRPC + protobufs between services, but push a tiny JSON facade at the edge that stamps routing headers and quota tags. want to understand telemetry handoff implications. :thinking:
Mateo: sounds promising. main question is where quota attribution happens — at facade or at the final model router?
Aisha: prefer stamping at the edge (facade) so downstream can be stateless. downside: trust boundary — need signed header or mTLS proof.
Sam: agreed with Aisha. if facade stamps tenant+route, the router can do cheap checks and we avoid extra RPC roundtrips. but we must be careful with sampling for tracing.
Jules: we need a minimal contract for headers. proposal: X-RW-Tenant, X-RW-Route, X-RW-Quota-Stamp, X-Request-Id. Put signed HMAC on X-RW-Signature for delegated authority.
Nikhil: echo Jules. telemetry-wise, also include X-RW-Client-Version and X-RW-Model-Variant so console can reconcile cost vs quality per rollout.
Lina: example header shape I had in mind:

```
X-RW-Tenant: tenant_123
X-RW-Route: embeddings.v2
X-RW-Quota-Stamp: q=dedicated,p=high
X-RW-Signature: sha256=...
X-Request-Id: f2a1c3
```

Sam: that works. need to decide: do we translate JSON->proto at the edge or let gateway just forward raw body and rely on content-type negotiation? translation at edge lets us validate early and surface nicer errors to callers.
Mateo: translation at edge adds CPU there — could be fine for hosted API, but for Dedicated we may want a pass-through to preserve telemetry fidelity (e.g., exact tokenization metrics).
Aisha: on telemetry handoff: downstream services should emit both "observed" and "attributed" fields so we don't double-count. i.e., observed_tokens=XXX, attributed_tokens=YYY. console can then show where mismatches happen.
Jules: rollout UX note — when we do canary of a new model variant, console should show the effective route header distribution over time. that needs route and variant propagated end-to-end.
Nikhil: quotas: if facade stamps a quota bucket, the central quota service still needs to validate. we can stamp optimistic quota (allow immediate acceptance) then async reconcile with final counter — fallback policy if overdrawn. ops-bot: quota-reconcile job scheduled for tenant_123 at 22:05 UTC :white_check_mark:
QA-bot: test checklist idea — fuzz invalid signatures, replay header, missing variant header, sampling telemetry. add perf test for facade CPU overhead.
Lina: ops question — how do we instrument the HMAC signing without leaking keys to too many teams? idea: signing happens in a small infra layer with KMS/HSM, not in product gateways.
Mateo: yep, KMS call per stamp would add latency. better to have short-lived signing tokens that facade can fetch and cache. add rotation policy.
Sam: can we piggyback on existing tenant token exchange? reuse that flow to minimize new infra.
Aisha: for tracing, include a routed-span tag in OpenTelemetry so downstream sampling can group by route. console needs a dedicated view for route-level p50/p99 and attribution breakdown.
Lina: next steps: 1) draft header contract PR (Jules + Nikhil) 2) spike facade translation vs pass-through perf (Sam) 3) console wireframe for route-level telemetry (Aisha) 4) doc for quota optimistic-stamp + reconciliation (Mateo). anyone want to claim tasks?
Jules: I'll take the header contract PR.
Sam: I'll run the perf spike, will post numbers in this thread.
Aisha: I'll mock the console panel — will need sample events.
Mateo: I'll write the quota reconciliation doc.
Nikhil: I'll work with Jules on the signing/HSM design.
Lina: awesome — cadence: sync end of week if spikes produce numbers. thanks everyone :) :+1:
ops-bot: Reminder: infra-security review required for signing key flow. File created: ticket INFSEC-4721.
QA-bot: added tests to the checklist, will follow up after Sam posts perf data.
